winner.title: Fish in Bangladeshi Shorshe Bata (Mustard Paste)

evidence.authenticity: Bangladeshi restaurant chef; shorshe bata paste with mustard oil and nigella is traditional, but written for generic fillets (ilish named as traditional, subs: bluefish, tilapia, shad, catfish) and adds lemon, cilantro and a pre-sauteed paste. Not a bone-in ilish steak curry.
evidence.precision: Only 1 of 10 ingredients has a weight; 4 steps, 4 with sensory cues (paste darkens and thickens, oil shimmering, consistency of cake batter); no temperatures or pan size ('large skillet').
evidence.testing: NYT Cooking editing, 39 ratings averaging 5; little explicit reasoning visible (paywalled).
evidence.photos: No step images in schema; process photos not confirmed.
evidence.efficiency: 30 minutes stated, realistic; paste is cooked first, then fish.
evidence.access: Mustard oil, nigella and yellow mustard seed are found at South Asian groceries; fish subs are given.

winner.why: Best precision, cues and test-kitchen editing of the five read, but it is a fillet adaptation and scores under 60.

runnerUp.title: Ilish Macher Sorshe bata diye Jhal | Shorshe Ilish | Hilsa Fish in Mustard Gravy

evidence.authenticity: Bengali author; soaked black and yellow mustard, strained paste, nigella, raw mustard oil finish; notes Bangal vs Ghoti variants and West Bengal and Bangladesh. West Bengal rather than Bangladeshi author.
evidence.precision: 6 pieces (~1 kg), 3.5 tbsp oil; times only, no doneness cues, no pan size ('deep pan').
evidence.testing: Few reasons given; sustainability advice (avoid khoka ilish under 600 g).
evidence.photos: One step photo (grinding paste); rest are finished shots.
evidence.access: No substitutions for hilsa or mustard oil.

runnerUp.why: Most traditional preparation, but time-only steps and almost no photos or reasoning.

searches: hilsa in mustard sauce Bengali recipe
notes: No candidate reached 60. Most recipes lack weights, pan sizes and doneness cues and have no process photos. Hilsa is sold frozen at Bangladeshi groceries in the US. The Bengali-language results (Prothom Alo, Bangla Tribune, ebanglalibrary) were not read. A retry could read those, or the Bongeats and Chittaranjan Park pages from search results.
